disposition: Accepted native R2 source and independent actual consumer boundary for public integration
findings: Read all five owned product/test/guide paths, including the full retained-report admission, path placement, native execution, result writer, console boundary, CLI dispatch and opt-in sandbox seam.

Saved success, diagnosis and model history remain historical metadata. The current sandbox result determines status; at least one retained case must pass and the selected existing suite must also satisfy the unchanged runner contract.

Report admission bounds bytes, file count and UTF-8 payload size; rejects duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, invalid Unicode/schema/path values; checks the descriptor after a nonblocking regular-file open.

Current retained test conflicts and symlink path components refuse before pytest. Exact matching regular files are reused in the private copy; missing saved files are written as exact UTF-8 bytes. The default generation path keeps its original write behavior.

Output paths are new and outside the checked repository. Input/setup/output errors remain exit 2, failed/no-retained-success execution is exit 1, and current success is exit 0. Partial result directories and console delivery failure are documented.

The final test-fixture-only revision imports the caller's pytest tooling through a .pth in a no-pip venv, matching the existing fixture contract without assuming a global pytest installation. All four other owned product blobs remain unchanged.

Two independent actual CLI calls supplied a disposable copy of the original saved report with forged passed/ok/final-success metadata and unchanged retained test bytes. The buggy checkout still returned exit 1 with 1 retained pass and 3 failures; the fixed checkout returned exit 0 with all 4 retained cases passed.

Both independent calls recorded historical status passed, zero model calls, exact original/forged report preservation, unchanged author and review fixtures, unchanged six runtime input pins, and empty stderr.

Reviewed authored R1 qualification and its actual read-only-file failure/repair; R2 preserves accepted timeout, generated-case collector and HTML-report owner inputs. No broad authored suite was repeated by root.
